blocks.text: Choose what you want to edit.
Open Setup and select your launcher Blueprint.
Click Use launcher's screen, roster & layout.
Choose a page on the left, then choose its editing target.
Check the asset path before making changes.
Click Save selected assets when finished.
Tip: Choosing an asset in Studio does not change what your game loads.

blocks.caption: Studio sidebar and the selected asset path

blocks.text: The wizard creates a connected selection screen.
Open New setup and leave Starter Screen empty.
Choose a name, folder and starter: Basic, animated 2D or 3D.
For the 3D starter, also choose a Preview Mesh.
Review the asset paths, then click Create setup.
Add characters to the new roster and save.
Place one generated launcher in your level, then press Play.
Tip: Use Starter Screen only when you want to copy an existing design.

blocks.caption: Setup wizard with the seven generated asset paths

blocks.text: Each fighter needs a character asset and a roster entry.
Click Create new character in Setup.
Give it a unique Character ID and a display name.
Assign Portrait for the slot and Large Portrait for the preview.
Add the asset on Roster and arrange the entries in your preferred order.
Save, then check the character in Live preview.
Tip: A locked character can be previewed when Allow Locked Slots is enabled, but cannot be selected.

blocks.caption: Character data beside its roster entry

blocks.text: Set the layout first, then choose how players move.
Open Grid layout to set columns, slot size and spacing.
Adjust Placement to position slots inside the grid container.
Open Navigation and choose Grid, Horizontal or Vertical.
Choose Wrap to loop at an edge, or Stop to stay there.
Compare Live preview and Play at the same screen size.
Tip: Move the whole grid in Designer if its parent layout is in the wrong place.

blocks.caption: Grid placement and navigation at the same viewport resolution

blocks.text: Style each part of the screen separately.
Open Slots, Character preview or Text & names.
Choose the image, border or text widget you want to change.
Edit its colors, font or alignment.
Choose its Layout slot for spacing, or open Designer to change the layout.
Tip: Shared widgets affect every screen using them; duplicate a widget when you need a separate design.

blocks.caption: Slot artwork and the shared player indicator in Designer

blocks.text: Players join by pressing a key or controller button.
Use Controls to change movement, confirm and cancel bindings.
Use Players & joining to set starting focus and CPU selection rules.
Use Join prompts to change the flashing message.
Add sounds and key icons under Sounds & button hints.
Test joining in Play; the join press is used only to join.
Remember: Each player needs a different device, and only one can use the keyboard. With CPU selection enabled, P1 chooses the opponent if P2 has not joined.

blocks.caption: Join prompts and two different devices joining

blocks.text: Slot motion shows which character each player is choosing.
Open Slot animations and choose your slot widget.
Try a preset such as Subtle, Pop or Lift.
Adjust scale, tint and timing for each state.
Use Idle for unused slots and Focused for the current cursor.
Check Selected and Shared states with both players on one slot.
Tip: Existing Blueprint animations restores your authored motion without deleting the timelines.

blocks.caption: Idle focused selected and shared slot states

blocks.text: Animate the portrait, name and subtitle separately.
Open Portrait & text animations and choose a player preview.
Try Fade, Slide or another preset.
Expand an element and adjust its Entrance and Exit settings.
Use Duration for speed and Delay for a later start.
Test character changes with Animation preview enabled.
Tip: The portrait and text swap together after the exit. If changes have no effect, check Animation sequencing for an override.

blocks.caption: Portrait name and subtitle entrance settings

blocks.text: Use artwork for 2D or a mesh for 3D.
For 2D, open 2D presentation and choose Static Artwork or Sprite Frames.
For frames, add textures in playback order and set the frame rate.
For 3D, choose the character on 3D presentation.
Set Preview Mode to Actor 3D and enable Override Presentation 3D.
Assign a mesh, then adjust the camera and lighting.
Use Add presentation host on the preview if its host is missing.
Test in Play; optional animation clips must match the mesh skeleton.
Tip: Character overrides replace the preview defaults for that fighter.

blocks.caption: 2D artwork and a framed 3D skeletal preview

blocks.text: Sequencing controls when the portrait and text appear.
Open Animation sequencing and choose a preview or character.
Try Together, Portrait first or Text first.
Adjust Group Gap to add a pause between the groups.
Choose Inherit to use the settings from the next level.
Priority: Character override, then player override, then shared sequence. Wait For Entrance delays the confirmation animation, not match travel.

blocks.caption: Sequence inheritance and portrait first timing

blocks.text: Try your layout and supported animations without starting Play.
Choose Player 1 or Player 2 and use the direction buttons.
Use Confirm and Cancel to check selection states.
Turn Animation preview on to see movement.
Use Pause and Step to inspect timing, or Reset to start again.
Use Play for real controllers, sounds, authored animation timing and custom Blueprint behavior.

blocks.caption: Live preview D-pad pause and step controls

blocks.text: A theme copies settings from one setup to another.
Select the source screen and layout, then create or choose a theme.
On Themes & presets, click Capture selected setup into theme.
Select the destination screen and layout, keeping the theme selected.
Choose the sections to apply, then apply, validate and save.
Tip: Slot Motion changes shared slot defaults. Themes do not copy widget layouts or animation timelines.

blocks.caption: Theme capture and the Apply sections checklist

blocks.text: Pass the chosen characters to your game.
Select your launcher and open Match handoff.
Enable Store Selection On Ready to keep both choices.
For level travel, enable Travel On Ready and choose a map.
Place a CharacterSelectMatchReceiver in that map to read the choices.
Include the destination map when packaging the game.
Your game must spawn the fighters and connect their gameplay controls.

blocks.caption: Launcher handoff and the destination receiver

blocks.text: Start with the setting closest to the problem.
Edits missing: check that Studio and the launcher use the same assets.
Layout different: compare the same resolution and inspect parent anchors.
Portrait missing: check artwork, opacity and the active presentation mode.
Animation unchanged: check the selected target and sequence overrides.
Click Validate setup, save, and restart Play.
Tip: Change one setting at a time so you can see what fixed the problem.

blocks.caption: Matching launcher references and preview fallback messages

blocks.text: Check the complete player experience before sharing.
Move both players onto one slot, then confirm and cancel.
Try keyboard, controllers, CPU selection and reconnection.
Check long names and portraits at your supported screen sizes.
Test match travel in a packaged game.

blocks.caption: A finished selection screen ready for acceptance testing
